# Native material RT port audit

Current candidate is not RT-qualified. Verified source paths:

- Exam/NativeU64/gfs_material_ssprk2_native.inc rejects nonzero GAS_ACCX/Y and accepts only gresho, kh, sod_periodic; requires single rank and periodic post stage.
- Exam/NativeU64/gfs_material_trace_probe.inc rejects is_ghost faces and requires periodic owner aliases. It writes hydrodynamic force/mass to acceleration, with no external source here.
- Exam/RT/rt.c uses rt_w2Measure2D, rt_evolBP, mkLinkedList2D_rt through existing blend integrators. Its checkpoint writer writes the common-prefix particle layout, not the extended native thermal/weight state: direct continuation requires a verified reader/writer contract.
- Exam/NativeU64/exam.c mkLinkedList2D_rt constructs boundary states with hydrostatic pressure adjustments. These cannot simply be aliased as periodic interior cells in the material transpose operator.

Required implementation sequence: extend existing boundary face assembly with explicit boundary work/force ledger and transpose-consistent pressure-volume operator; preserve physical wall constraints and full native checkpoint fields; add external gravity source once at the correct integration layer and track potential energy or external work; verify unperturbed hydrostatic equilibrium before seeded RT. Retain fixed mass, convexity and weight constraint checks. Do not merely remove runtime guards. No RT evolution is claimed by this audit. 3D remains deferred until 2D qualification.

# RT sidecar to SoA owner resolution

Added shared Exam/gfs_material_rt_owner.h and replaced the duplicated native RT owner typedef. The resolver builds an O(n) ID hash and maps each padding slot to a current owned SoA index. It validates x periodic translations, y reflections about the actual supplied walls, duplicate owned IDs, metadata count and owner existence. Ghost particle IDs retain MAX_INDEX; reflected owners come from the sidecar. The resolver does not modify particle state.

The exact existing RT boundary-builder fixture is rerun using native particle types and the new shared header. Across three rebuilds including permuted IDs, all 60 padding entries, 36 mirrors and 12 periodic/reflected corners resolve correctly. Previous physical boundary checks remain unchanged (maximum error 8.88e-16). Added negative tests reject stale counts, duplicate IDs and wrong periodic-image coordinates.

This validates conversion of boundary metadata to the array order used by fillParticleSoA. The resolver is not yet consumed by the material RHS bridge, whose periodic guards remain. It does not qualify GPU wall tessellation or RT evolution. Next wiring must retain actual wall geometry and boundary-aware pressure/velocity trace maps, and must not invoke periodic-only gpu_unified_owner_aliases on reflected ghosts.

# Native RT trace bridge

The native material bridge now accepts reflected-wall metadata. The RT diagnostic wrapper resolves sidecar IDs against current SoA IDs, avoiding the periodic-only alias resolver for mirror ghosts. The same metadata is passed to the CSR reconstruction, weight-rate solve and active projection. The reconstruction limiter now supports even scalar ghosts and odd normal velocity; the original periodic API delegates with NULL metadata. RT sidecar capture is enabled by either MATERIAL_EVOLVE or MATERIAL_TRACE_PROBE.

Both native C/MPI translation units compile on syntax. A 64-cell nonuniform weighted periodic-x/bounded-y fixture constructs the native SoA/FaceCSR inputs and calls the actual bridge implementation. Direct operator results agree within 1.879e-16 with thermo-only limiting on/off; the full velocity-limiter build is also tested in results.json. This tests host array wiring with controlled geometry, not CUDA tessellation or a production RT run.

The public RT apply path deliberately remains rejected: compatible gravity, time/potential ledger, boundary update and checkpoint integration are not yet connected. Existing native periodic guards are retained. Geometry supplied by CUDA still needs inspection before any RT time evolution. Fixed walls must map to the owner's own reflected image; unsupported reflected-other-owner faces fail explicitly.

# Compatible gravity in native material diagnostic bridge

The native bridge now computes exact polygon volume centroids from directed face geometry (face area, normal and midpoint), checks cell closure and agreement with native volume, and calls the shared compatible gravity RHS. No volume quadrature or new physical parameter is introduced. The public RT wrapper passes grad(Phi)=-acceleration and retains the explicit evolution rejection until time integration/ledger wiring is qualified. A nonzero linear potential in periodic x is rejected. Active constraints use the gravity-aware projection in the internal implementation.

Tests: the actual bridge implementation on controlled 64-cell SoA/FaceCSR input agrees with direct gravity/hydro calls to 4.529e-16 across gravity off/on and thermo limiting off/on. Gravity runs have total power residuals at most 1.364e-14. Independent polygon clipping of 16 irregular weighted partitions (16 cells each) agrees with native centroids to 6.315e-16; wrong supplied volumes are rejected. Native C/MPI main and extraction translation units compile.

Scope: the bridge fixture supplies controlled face geometry; it is not a GPU tessellation test. Internal apply is exercised for array writeback comparison, but public RT time evolution remains disabled. No performance comparison, MPI gravity qualification, 3D validation or KH/RT completion follows from these results. The new centroid helper and power coupling are not an acceleration kick; the native adapter must not apply the old external kick on top.

# Actual native CUDA geometry with RT-style mirrors

An isolated C/MPI fixture links the existing native exam_gpu.o from the thermo-only library and calls gpu_init, particle/cell upload, gpu_tessellate_and_build_faces, tessellation/face download, then the current host material gravity bridge. It uses A10 GPU1 on syntax, leaving the existing KH job on GPU0. No Python hydro or replacement tessellator is used. Unused trajectory/force-link callbacks fail fast; circle attestation returns false. This is not a complete production-executable run.

Aligned 16x16 cells produce 1280 raw face records, of which 32 nonzero faces are own reflected wall faces. Initial counting included 16 zero-length reflected-other faces; applying the SAME existing 1e-12 edge exclusion used by the production bridge leaves none. No exclusion threshold or physics coefficient was changed. The aligned hydrostatic acceleration residual is 1.943e-15.

A second fixture jitters generators and assigns nonzero varying weights. Native CUDA produces 1525 face records with 32 nonzero own-reflected wall faces, no invalid neighbors and no nonzero reflected-other faces. Cell mass/internal energy are initialized once from actual CUDA volumes and volume centroids to uniform density and P=2-0.5*ycentroid. Gravity+hydro bridge succeeds; maximum hydrostatic acceleration is 8.777e-12, total power residual 7.476e-25. `max_volume_difference_from_uniform` measures the intended changed cell sizes, NOT a geometric error. Closure and volume consistency are checked separately by the centroid helper.

These are frozen geometry/force tests, not RT time evolution. Images are constructed directly for controlled geometry, while native RT builder ownership was verified in prior fixtures; end-to-end native driver and MPI boundary integration remain pending. No CUDA hydro-force parity or GIZMO runtime claim.

# RT short evolution using existing native operators

This isolated C/MPI runner calls the existing native CUDA tessellator, current C material gravity bridge, and existing GfsMaterialStepState SSPRK2 stage update. It is an integration test of these components, not the production native simulation driver (which still rejects RT evolution). Image/padding refresh is controlled by the fixture; all cell forces, weight rates and thermal rates come from the shared operators. No new hydro solver, gravity kick, viscosity or thermal repair is introduced.

Initial condition: periodic-x unit square, reflecting fixed y walls, 16x16 regular cells, density 1 below y=0.5 and 2 above, g_y=-0.5, continuous piecewise-linear hydrostatic P, and optional vy=0.001*cos(2*pi*x)*sin(pi*y). Initial interface coincides with cell faces. Fixed per-cell masses; actual CUDA volume/centroid at every RHS; positive U/V, in-domain y, geometric validity and a conservative acoustic step bound are checked. Checkpoints here are diagnostic CSV states, not the production checkpoint format.

An initial build accidentally inherited the older angular reconstruction metric from initial_compile.json. Its retained rest/dt1/dt2/dt4 results give approximately first-order temporal self-convergence (0.996) and are NOT the current candidate. No results were deleted. The corrected build explicitly sets GFS_MATERIAL_FACE_MEASURE_LS and GFS_MATERIAL_THERMO_LIMIT_ONLY. Its face_rest/face_dt1/face_dt2/face_dt4 results reach t=0.02; dt=0.001,0.0005,0.00025 give velocity differences 1.561e-10 and 3.982e-11 (order1.971). Total-energy relative errors <=1.72e-15; per-cell masses unchanged. The rest case stays at max speed3.853e-17.

This establishes short-time integration consistency, not RT growth accuracy, spatial convergence, nonlinear mixing, MPI/CUDA hydro-force parity or the GIZMO runtime goal. The solve/force work in this runner is host C; geometry is actual CUDA. End-to-end production wiring remains pending.

Continuation: both perturbed runs resume the identical face_dt4 t=0.02 CSV (SHA recorded per run), rather than restarting. They reach t=0.2 with dt0.001/0.0005; rest resumes its own t=0.02 state. See extension_comparison.json for measured residuals. The printed seed parameter in resumed jobs is the unused initialization argument; actual state is entirely restored from the recorded source, including the unperturbed rest case.

# RT spatial-resolution and limiter continuation

Uses the same isolated native C/MPI/CUDA component runner as material_rt_gpu_evolution_20261106_v1, built at N16 and N32 with FACE_MEASURE_LS and THERMO_LIMIT_ONLY. Baseline runs leave LIMIT_MAPS disabled, and explicitly labelled limited branches enable it only after restoring the common t0.5 state. This isolates late limiter effects, not a complete limited-method trajectory from t0.

N16 resumes its existing t0.2 state; N32 starts once at its new spatial resolution, then resumes its own t0.2 and t0.5 states. Every restart records source SHA. Both baseline runs reach t1. Boundary faces separating original lower/upper cell IDs are saved; eight-point Gaussian integration computes the interface Fourier displacement directly along actual straight cell faces, rather than estimating it from generator positions. The signed modes, projected interface length, mean displacement, positive U/V and energy residuals are saved in interface_metrics.json.

This controlled sharp-interface RT initialization is not the existing paper's smoothed RT setup. Agreement between two coarse resolutions is evidence of consistency, not proof of physical growth accuracy. A continuum/reference growth calculation and more spatial resolutions remain needed. MPI decomposition, native production checkpoint/driver wiring, full CUDA force execution, and the GIZMO runtime target remain unqualified. All source states/results are retained.

## Measured growth and limitation at t3

Both native CUDA-geometry/C-force component runs continue from checkpoints to t3 at dt0.0005. The independently derived compressible interfacial mode has growth1.05057676538; spatial ODE tolerance refinement agrees to2.2e-14 and the high-pressure limit agrees with the finite-depth incompressible formula to2.5e-6 absolute.

Measured ln(eta3/eta2) is1.05416965605 at N16 and1.06827224647 at N32: reference differences0.342% and1.684%. This is NOT monotonic convergence toward the reference. After optimal scalar normalization, the combined horizontal/vertical velocity Fourier profile differs from the growing eigenmode by17.8%/19.4%. Initial sinusoidal velocity is not a pure eigenmode, so this does not isolate numerical error. At t3 k*eta is0.054/0.057, small but not zero. No physical-accuracy pass is declared.

Next discriminating IC: keep the same flat interface, hydrostatic rho/P, fixed initial masses and W0, but prescribe the derived modal horizontal/vertical velocities. The equal growing/decaying pair has initial zero displacement/pressure/density perturbation, so linear theory gives eta(t)=(v_interface0/s)*sinh(s*t). This removes unrelated acoustic initial transients without introducing a new physical term, sensor or coefficient. Compare both resolutions against the full time-dependent modal prediction and retain the existing trajectories.

## Frozen t=1 force decomposition (32² and 64²)

Artifact: `Research/MaterialVolume_20261105/material_rt_force_audit_20261106_v1`.
Native CUDA geometry / host material RHS snapshots were exported without evolving the saved states. Opt-in exports retain the actual limited maps and canonical directed faces. Standalone native C decomposition evaluates pressure `C^T P`, potential contribution `B^T eta - gx - C^T eta`, and cached acoustic dissipation, with `eta=L^+gW`. No physical coefficient or evolution state was changed.

The sum matches the common gravity operator to 6.09e-18 (32²) and 2.94e-18 (64²); comparison to the independently exported execution RHS is within 1.44e-17 and 8.67e-18. The horizontal fundamental acceleration differs from the linear modal reference by relative L2 25.72% and 39.20%; 98.73% and 95.47% of its squared residual lies in the four interface-adjacent rows. These are instantaneous accelerations, not the previously reported velocity errors.

At 64², row30 has pressure+gravity acceleration -0.00103380 versus reference -0.00105669, but acoustic dissipation adds -0.00123927. At row31 the pressure+gravity value is -0.00494095 versus reference -0.00116009, and dissipation +0.00441739 largely cancels it. Corresponding opposite-sign behavior occurs above the interface. Thus removal of dissipation alone is not supported: adjacent rows exhibit both excess conservative forcing and compensating dissipation, while the next rows receive excess dissipative forcing.

This frozen evolved state establishes where the current force resides, not the origin of the earlier velocity error. Next discriminate interface reconstruction/limiter effects and the potential-gradient coupling on the same frozen geometry before changing any physical model. Reference samples remain linear-mode row samples, not exact evolving-cell averages. Production MPI/CUDA force equivalence, full 2D acceptance, and GIZMO runtime qualification remain incomplete.

`material_rt_force_audit_20261106_v1/limiter_screen.py` creates separate diagnostic copies of the exported t=1 states, modifying only specified reconstruction alpha arrays. No time evolution or production setting is changed. Every variant retains the same geometry, cell state, force/work adjoints, and potential coupling.

Horizontal fundamental acceleration relative L2 versus linear reference:

| N | Baseline | Unlimited density | Unlimited pressure | Unlimited both thermodynamic fields | First-order velocity |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 0.257213 | 0.254758 | 0.257213 | 0.254758 | 1.321926 |
| 64 | 0.392004 | 0.422341 | 0.392004 | 0.422341 | 2.424410 |

Velocity reconstruction is already unlimited in both snapshots. Pressure limiter removal has no measurable force effect in this screen; density limiter removal does not consistently improve the force. This rules out a simple limiter-toggle fix at this state, not an influence of limiter history during evolution. Need examine the underlying cross-interface reconstruction and compatible potential force, not add an arbitrary limiter coefficient. These tests do not establish nonlinear time-evolution stability for the diagnostic variants.

### Face-level acoustic jump and interface geometry

Diagnostic `face_trace.c` reproduces the actual cached reconstruction and effective pressure `P-eta` on every canonical face. The identity `sum A[(jp)^2/(ZL+ZR)+ZL ZR/(ZL+ZR)*(jv)^2] = sum H` holds exactly at 32² and to 2.52e-22 at 64². This validates the face-level heat accounting against the common operator, not continuum entropy correctness.

At 32², velocity-jump heat is 5.718e-8 and pressure-jump heat 8.402e-9. At 64² these are 6.153e-8 and 1.246e-9. Faces between the original lower/upper material labels account for 71.71% and 89.83% of velocity-jump heat. Their reconstructed normal-jump RMS is 2.099e-4 / 2.415e-4; the horizontal velocity projection contributes RMS 2.129e-4 / 2.431e-4, compared with vertical contributions 1.460e-5 / 1.541e-5.

The same labelled interface has total length 1.01517 / 1.03347 and area-weighted horizontal normal RMS 0.16156 / 0.24008. ### Opt-in current-material face CFL

Added a diagnostic crossing-time calculation to the material adapter after the
actual Wdot solution. For each owner face, compute geometric normal speed from
generator velocities, face offset, and (Wdot_i-Wdot_j)/(2d); reflected walls
have zero boundary speed. Signal is max(c_i+|v_i.n-w_n|,c_j+|v_j.n-w_n|).
The candidate bound is Courant*min_i[V_i/sum_faces(A*signal)]. Uniform boosts
cancel algebraically in the relative speeds. This is a conservative geometric
crossing-time candidate, NOT a proven stability bound for the entire nonlocal
material operator; evolved comparisons remain necessary.

instead of the legacy force-kernel/weight-oscillator bound. Existing kernel

selection keeps the legacy bound. Invalid crossing data reject, not clip.

`work_decomposition.py` exactly decomposes delta H (H=Udot+Pcell Vdot) into volume-work, pressure-force-work, and the bilinear correction −sum A delta(pstar) delta(ustar), at fixed physical state. Max|delta pstar|/original pstar=53366.97 and max|delta ustar|=17.00995 on this frozen state: the frozen-impedance linear response is being used far beyond a small correction. Do NOT delete the cross term: it is part of conservative total pressure work. Existing Kepler's variational force/adiabatic-volume identity is still a consistency reference; earlier pressure-limited reversible map(mode2) fails continuity and is not revived. Native direct constrained implementation remains unadopted. Need a physically justified nonlinear closure or different compatible geometric evolution, not a new sensor/thermal clipping patch.

## 2026-11-07: dimension-independent minimum-change gradient prototype

Objective, for each scalar cell reconstruction: minimize 0.5 ||g-g0||^2 subject to lower_f <= q_i + r_f dot g <= upper_f. Geometry supplies r_f (face centroid relative to volume centroid); existing neighbor extrema and wall positivity supply bounds. Zero gradient is feasible. One common gradient describes every face. No new physical coefficient or sensor. In 1D this is interval projection of a slope; the identical algorithm accepts dimensions 1 through 3.

`project.h` implements a small primal active-set solve, at most dim independent constraints, explicit failure on singular/nonfinite geometry or iteration exhaustion. Tolerances scale with machine epsilon, not physical tuning. Normalized rows are required. This is an isolated research prototype, not a production default or an update to shared global context.

Tests found and fixed roundoff in the full-rank active set: its feasible tangent space is exactly zero; treating a rounded nonzero direction as physical caused a false failure. Final checks passed. This is algebra, NOT 3D hydro evolution, and elapsed Python test time is not a solver benchmark.

## 2026-11-07: pressure-acceleration reconstruction

# Density-aware pressure reconstruction experiment

Let ri = xf-ci and rj = xf-cj = ri-dij for a shared face and volume centroids. A local approximation with common h=grad(P)/rho gives continuity Pi+rhoi h dot ri = Pj+rhoj h dot rj. Therefore Pj-Pi = grad(P)i dot [ri-(rhoj/rhoi)rj]. Use this effective displacement ONLY in the pressure least-squares fit; retain geometric metric weights, density reconstruction, closest-gradient bounds, velocity reconstruction, Riemann solver, conservative face force/work, fixed masses and point gravity unchanged.

No explicit gravity, equilibrium pressure template, cell-specific parameter or threshold enters this formula. Equal density returns the original separation bitwise, not merely approximately. Constant pressure gives zero fit RHS even for unequal density. The approximation is local to reconstruction; it does NOT impose equal pressure acceleration throughout the fluid, nor add pressure acceleration as a new evolved variable. On irregular contact geometry tangential acceleration accuracy still needs tests.

Opt-in macro GFS_MATERIAL_PRESSURE_ACCELERATION, used with projected thermodynamics. Default scalar and projected-only variants remain available. ## 2026-11-07: native frozen force decomposition

Previous goal turn: progress. Same-phase history comparison proved a real early RT regression, changing the next action from extension/adoption to operator diagnosis.

Built native_force_audit from the current candidate with diagnostic-only instrumentation; production hydro headers unchanged. Ran three frozen snapshots (original t0, current half-dt accepted t=.3, previous support method accepted t=.3) with CURRENT candidate operator. All exited normally BEFORE time update; C/CUDA RHS parity max absolute3.47e-18. Source/binary hashes in force_audit_sources.json. No new time trajectory or 3D evolution.

Exact material Riemann decomposition at each interior face: pstar = alpha_right*P_left + alpha_left*P_right - stress, stress=Z_left*alpha_right*(uR_n-uL_n). Thus owner force decomposes into -A*pbar*n and +A*stress*n. This is an identity evaluated with original wave impedances; because those impedances depend on the full Riemann solution, the pieces are NOT independent counterfactual solutions with a term disabled. No force term was disabled.

Initial interface horizontal modal acoustic accelerations approximately(+1.023e-6,-.754e-6), pressure part roundoff. At current accepted half-dt t=.3, interface rows give pressure(-2.073e-4,+1.486e-4), acoustic(+8.269e-4,-4.202e-4), total(+6.196e-4,-2.716e-4). Linear reference accelerations(-2.962e-4,+3.097e-4). Acoustic contribution dominates and reverses the sign of total horizontal acceleration at these rows. Projection uses initial particle x phases and initial row labels, consistently across cases.

Applying the SAME CURRENT operator to the OLD support-method t=.3 state gives pressure(-.857e-4,+2.091e-4), acoustic(+1.168e-3,-5.912e-4), total(+1.082e-3,-3.821e-4). This is not the old operator's actual RHS; it is a frozen-state transfer test. It shows the reversed acceleration need not arise solely from the new trajectory's accumulated time-integration errors. Reference comparison remains linear-mode evidence, not proof of every nonlinear error source.

Horizontal component sum agrees with full native acceleration to maximum1.13e-11 (large background-pressure cancellation). Wall forces are excluded from the decomposition; wall normals have zero x component in these planar-wall cases. Vertical decomposition therefore is not the complete gravity/wall budget and must NOT be interpreted as such.

Source difference matters: historical transpose form distributes force through matching reconstruction adjoints; direct FV applies pstar forces only to two face owners. Therefore the two schemes differ in force assembly as well as reconstruction, gravity quadrature and acceptance/timestep machinery. Current evidence does not isolate all of these changes or justify blindly returning to the older method.

Next discriminating task: determine whether the acoustic owner force at the contact comes predominantly from faces crossing the material density interface and whether reconstruction/adjoint force distribution accounts for the older scheme's smaller error, while retaining conservation and dimensional consistency. Do not add a shear sensor, tune viscosity, or disable acoustic forces on this evidence alone. All diagnostic runs terminal; goal incomplete, 2D first, no runtime<=2x GIZMO claim.

Scope: this promotes an already supported fixed-plane relation into the
actual existing code and removes duplicated axis assumptions. It does NOT
solve the cylinder's cross-owner ghost faces or moving polygonal wall. For
a stationary plane n.x=b, xghost=x-2(n.x-b)n and vghost=(I-2nn^T)v; equal W
fixes the common bisector and its normal speed is0. A circle's radial mirror
is different: xghost-c=(2R/r-1)(x-c), whose derivative is
-v_normal*n+(2R/r-1)*v_tangent, while the reflected fluid velocity is
-v_normal*n+v_tangent. Their distinction and the cross-owner curved faces
remain essential for the upcoming cylinder boundary integration. Do not
merely label radial ghosts as zero-work planar walls, discard cross faces, or
use the legacy position/velocity postStage correction as a conservative pass.

### Why the original open boundary cannot simply be enabled in material RHS

For a planar original self-image, xghost=2*xb-xowner and Wghost=Wowner.
Consequently its face is fixed at xb and its geometric normal speed is zero,
including when both weights change. The material Riemann face, however,
has volume flux A*u_star; an ordinary open flow has u_star != 0.
This is not remedied by changing the ghost's mesh velocity to its fluid
velocity, which would no longer differentiate the geometry being used.

An explicit common-Riemann check gives total boundary volume target 0 for
balanced unit inflow/outflow, but +0.2 for unit inflow and speed-1.2 outflow
(unit measures, equal rho and P). The sum of geometric volume changes of a
fixed box remains zero. Internal/periodic faces cancel from the sum; removing
the radial image contribution on both sides leaves the same necessary open
compatibility condition. Thus a uniform-stream pass alone is insufficient.

In particular, putting open ghosts into the current `image_owner` array
would turn them into walls, while treating their copied Wdot as prescribed
zero would differentiate the wrong geometry. Subtracting the incompatible
mean from the target would also change the physical problem. None of those
substitutions has been implemented. The original penetration treatment
remains valid for reuse; an opening must instead represent the passage of
material consistently with the ownership/inflow/outflow bookkeeping. This
boundary issue must be resolved before claiming a native RunCylinder material
evolution or launching its refinement comparison.

Read-only review found two gaps in the initial device test, both corrected
in `device_coverage_v2`: periodic translations are now tested in both
directions (512 each), and near-contact high+low coordinates must recover
the correct image normal. Across 61 near-contact cases, 60 have nonzero low
parts and the maximum normal error is 2.29e-16; host/device difference remains
4.00e-15. This check would reject losing all low parts in oblique near-contact
images, unlike the earlier absolute-coordinate-only tolerance. Initial test
artifacts were preserved and the manifest identifies the revised source.

`wall_support_v1` implements a candidate-completeness correction in the
existing native C/CUDA path. Every actual cell vertex must lie in its owner's
outward tangent halfspace, a sufficient certificate for the entire convex
cell, including edges. At each geometry evaluation the original4h seed is
built, missing equal-weight self images are added, and the same x/v/m/U/W
state is retessellated before AoS volume writeback. Requests are local to this
state, not accumulated across time. Added sites shrink existing real power
cells, so one batch suffices in exact arithmetic; the second geometry must
still pass the certificate. Both SSP stages, endpoint and restart/ownership
refresh use this path. Pressure/work formulas and the contact ledger do not
